newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's PRI faces tough fight in state elections.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's PRI faces tough fight in state elections.

text.p: Opinion polls show Mexico's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) will face a tough challenge in forthcoming local elections, the daily newspaper Reforma reported on Monday.

Reforma conducted the polls in four municipalities in the state of Mexico, which adjoins Mexico City and where elections for mayor and the state legislature will be held on Nov. 10. Mayors in all four municipalities currently belong to the PRI.

The four, Ecatepec, Nezahualcoyotl, Naucalpan and Tlalnepantla, are the largest in the state and have a joint population of more than four million and account for 36 percent of the state's population. The state of Mexico is the country's most populous with 11.7 million people.

Reforma said 500 people in each city were polled Oct. 11-15 but did not report the margin of error. The polls show the PRI ahead in Ecatepec and Nezahualcoyotl but losing Naucalpan and Tlalnepantla to the conservative National Action Party (PAN).
The leftist Democratic Revolution Party (PRD) polled third in all four, except Nezahualcoyotl, where it was tied for second place with the PAN.
The PRI's advantage was 24 to 19 percent in Ecatapec and just 25 to 23 percent in Nezahuacoyotl. It trailed by 27 to 32 percent in Naucalpan and 30 to 31 percent in Tlalnepantla.

At the national level, the PRI has held the presidency since it was formed in 1929 and still holds a majority of state governorships and in both houses of congress. But the PAN in recent years has won several state governorships from the PRI and is the second largest party group in congress.
